bottom_line: The recommendation stands: publish from TIGER/Line 2026, and keep the Montana State Library roads out of any public product unless MSL grants written permission. TIGER terms are explicit and verified verbatim in the live ISO metadata of the roads, ADDR and EDGES files. MSL terms are a disclaimer with "for no other purpose", no licence grant, and MSL asserts its name as copyright text and credit in its live ArcGIS service. Most worker figures reproduce: statewide and county counts, all 56 county zip sizes, TIGER class lengths, the Billings and Benchland TIGER counts, and the Billings geometry agreement on live MSL geometry. Several figures need correction: placeholder counts, one address-field definition, the speed-limit count, overlap percentages that depend on how junctions are counted, the Benchland duplicate and road-overlap wording, a stitched legal quote, and the claim that no attribution line exists. None of these changes the choice.

recommendation_note: The recommendation stands. Legal basis: the TIGER terms (not copyrighted; free to use in a product or publication; acknowledge the U.S. Census Bureau as the source; no access constraint) are verified verbatim in the live roads, ADDR and EDGES metadata. The MSL metadata gives a disclaimer ("for no other purpose"), no licence grant, and MSL asserts its name as copyright text and credit, so MSL-derived tiles should not be published without written permission. Technical basis: on live MSL geometry the two sources agree in Billings (98.5 percent of MSL length within 15 m of TIGER; 94.6 percent the other way), so the choice is legal and cleaning-driven, not geometric. TIGER overlaps (13 to 22 percent in Billings; 66 to 75 percent in Benchland, depending on junction handling) are real and need cleaning; MSL overlap is 0.4 to 7 percent. The step the recommendation left untested now checks out: every ADDR TLID joins to Yellowstone EDGES (100 percent), and 99.2 percent of matches carry a street name. The 400 North 27th sample gives the same answer in both sources: the nearest segments are 40 to 47 m away and the MSL 400-block segment is about 260 m away, so an address point source is still needed to test the address match.
